investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T08:27–08:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the scheduling step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free any slots, every new remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers pod creation; because the pod never schedules, no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain missing.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error with latencyMs=147306, confirming a third independent pod creation attempt also failed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-ready state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs of 154428 is within the outage window, confirming a hard failure.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), amplifying the impact of any capacity exhaustion on those nodes.

Tertiary: A prior remote agent pod or set of pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (e.g., stuck in a non-terminal state), preventing new allocations. Preemption found no victims (failed-check.message), which is consistent with all existing holders being non-preemptible.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady, or resource quota change) may have reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots below the level needed to serve concurrent probe runs. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm this.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at approximately 08:29–08:34 UTC on 2026-06-25 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the probe pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were ever written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node is eligible for scheduling. The probe pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–149 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevented agent creation entirely; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T08:27–08:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the scheduling step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free any slots, every new remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers pod creation; because the pod never schedules, no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain missing.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154428, pod was stuck unscheduled for 149s before the check timed out and failed.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with latencyMs=153715, confirming the condition persisted across a second independent pod creation attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error with latencyMs=147306, confirming a third independent pod creation attempt also failed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-ready state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod; no evidence is written until the agent reaches a ready state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs of 154428 is within the outage window, confirming a hard failure.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), amplifying the impact of any capacity exhaustion on those nodes.

Tertiary: A prior remote agent pod or set of pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (e.g., stuck in a non-terminal state), preventing new allocations. Preemption found no victims (failed-check.message), which is consistent with all existing holders being non-preemptible.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady, or resource quota change) may have reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots below the level needed to serve concurrent probe runs. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm this.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-25 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected because the agent VM pod never left the pending state, making it impossible for the eval runner to reach the remote runtime and satisfy the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every createAgent call in the eval runner stalls until the probe timeout fires (~141–149 s), returning an Unschedulable error instead of a running VM. Because the pod never starts, no runtime response is produced and all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remain missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=147306, pod stuck unscheduled for 141s before probe timeout.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=154428, pod stuck 149s — same scheduling failure on an earlier check in the same run.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=153715, pod stuck 145s — confirms the condition persisted across sequential checks.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent because the pod never reached a running state.
failed-check.evidence: empty object — zero evidence collected, consistent with a pre-start infrastructure failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId; a scheduling failure at this call would prevent all downstream evidence collection.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latency of 147306ms is well within the outage threshold, confirming the probe timed out on the scheduling wait rather than a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity existed elsewhere it would be unreachable. This could be a pre-existing constraint or a recent node label change.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: all three checks ran sequentially within the same observability window (ending at 08:29, 08:32, 08:34) and each encountered the same exhaustion, suggesting the cluster was not sized to absorb even a single eval pod at the time of the run.

Lower confidence — transient spike in production remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots just before the eval window: no workload or traffic signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Observe whether the pod scheduling error recurs or the check passes.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the cluster-level capacity constraint is still present.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to check the allocatable and requested counts for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on each node that carries it.

reproductionSteps.label: Check node labels on all 6 nodes against the pod's affinity/selector spec
reproductionSteps.details: Verify whether the 4 non-kata nodes have ever matched the affinity rules, or whether a label change has narrowed the eligible set.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent VM scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that carry this resource, blocking all remote agent pod creation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only the 2 exhausted kata nodes (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same underlying scheduling error, indicating the entire feature's eval surface is blocked (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; a scheduling failure at this point prevents all subsequent evidence collection (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether existing workloads are holding all VM slots and whether any can be safely evicted or scaled down.

Review the pod's node affinity/selector rules to confirm whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional; if not, assess whether those nodes can be made eligible by adding the required labels or relaxing the selector.
Assess whether the cluster needs additional kata-capable nodes provisioned to handle concurrent eval probes alongside production remote-agent workloads.

Check whether the remote-agents feature's degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188) have triggered a feature-level degraded or outage status, and communicate accordingly to stakeholders if so.
Once capacity is restored or nodes are added, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks to confirm the scheduling error is resolved and all required evidence fields are collected.

Consider adding a pre-flight cluster capacity check to the eval runner that reports a SKIP or WARN status with a clear capacity message rather than waiting for the full pod-scheduling timeout (~141-149s) to expire.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity constraint is still present or has resolved since the failing run at 08:34 UTC.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling failure persists across the full remote-agents feature check suite.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity via cluster tooling
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the capacity exhaustion hypothesis without requiring another full eval run.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe nodes (or equivalent) filtered to nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to read allocatable vs. requested counts.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels against pod affinity/selector spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out a node label misconfiguration as a contributing or independent cause of the scheduling failure.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Compare the node selector and affinity rules in the remote agent pod spec against current node labels on all 6 nodes to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or a drift.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run local-agent-runtime eval probe as a control
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If local-agent-runtime passes, the failure is isolated to the remote kata peer-pod scheduling path and not a broader API, token, or org-resolution issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all pass would indicate the capacity constraint was transient and has self-resolved.

kubectl describe node output showing non-zero free kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was misleading or the resource accounting was stale.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was intentionally changed to exclude the 4 non-kata nodes as part of a planned migration would reframe the 4-node exclusion as expected behavior rather than a misconfiguration.

A passing run of the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks at the same timestamp would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote (kata peer-pod) scheduling path and not a broader API or credential issue.

Cluster autoscaler or node-provisioner logs showing a new kata-capable node was added and the pod was subsequently scheduled would confirm the root cause was pure capacity exhaustion rather than a selector mismatch.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all eligible nodes and warns when free slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add a cluster node-affinity coverage check that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.
Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote agent pod and fires a warning before the full probe timeout is reached, enabling faster detection of capacity pressure.

Consider a sibling-correlation eval rule: if all checks under a single feature fail with the same Unschedulable message within the same run window, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency investigation rather than treating each check independently.

evidenceDigest.message: pod stuck unscheduled for 141s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
